decisions.claim: B is a cable/service provider who has packages to offer
decisions.reason: Turn 3 'What packages do you have?' presupposes B has packages; turn 1 'I want to get some cable' contextualizes B as a cable/service provider. Solid E2 presupposition from A's questions directed at B.
decisions.counterexample: B could be a reseller or intermediary rather than the primary provider, but still qualifies as someone who has packages to offer.

decisions.reason: c2 'B offers/sells cable packages' is a weaker projection of c1 'B is a cable/service provider who has packages to offer.' Both derive from the same presupposition in turn 3. c1 is the more complete representative.

decisions.claim: B has a package that includes basic and movie channels
decisions.reason: Turn 7 asks 'Is there a package with basic and movie channels?' and turn 9 says 'Let me get that package,' presupposing such a package exists and B has it. A's selection confirms the package was available from B.
decisions.counterexample: A might have been mistaken about what 'that package' referred to, but the sequential logic strongly presupposes B had the package.

decisions.claim: B has additional offerings beyond the package A selected
decisions.reason: Turn 5 'What else have you got?' presupposes B has additional offerings beyond what was already discussed. This is a distinct claim from c1/c2 about B's broader inventory.
decisions.counterexample: A might have asked generically without knowing B had more, but the phrasing 'what else' presupposes additional items exist.

decisions.claim: B is a cable service provider or sales representative
decisions.reason: c5 'B is a cable service provider or sales representative' is essentially the same role attribution as c1, derived from the same evidence (turns 1 and 3). c1 is the more complete formulation.
